text:
Maria G.: Quick sync — dropping a strawman for an 'Inference Efficiency Guidance' roadmap that combines batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization recommendations, and eval-triggered alerts. Looking for feedback on scope and launch gates.
Sam Li: Love the consolidation. Can we explicitly call out which customer asks drive MVP? we should prioritize high-frequency token workloads and mobile clients.
Maria G.: Yeah — MVP = three features: 1) per-route batching suggestions + autoset, 2) prefix/KV cache hints with TTL heuristics, 3) quantization profiles suggestion (FP16/INT8) + fallback policy. Eval alerts are alpha gating.
Jordan Green: Suggestion: make quant recommendations opt-in per-customer. risk of quality regressions. tie quant recs to eval buckets and a rollback plan.
Lee: +1. Also need cost/latency delta estimator in the UI so SEs can see econ impact before enabling. even a rough p99/p50 delta is fine.
Alice K: For launch criteria, propose: (a) integration tests for correctness with quantized variants, (b) pilot with 3 customers (one mobile, one chat, one embedding-heavy), (c) alerting for eval regression with >5% drop on golden-vignettes.
Sam Li: Minor nit — make the pilot customers optional for GA if we can hit SLI targets in internal e2e and a beta cohort. Customers can be used to de-risk but shouldn't block GA if infra is stable.
Maria G.: Good call. Draft launch gates I had in mind:
```
Gates:
  - infra_stable: p99 latency within SLA across sample workload
  - correctness: unit + integration tests pass for quant variants
  - econ_estimator: cost delta shown in Console for top 5 routes
  - eval_alerts_alpha: eval-triggered alerting implemented (alpha)
  - pilot_validation: at least 1 external pilot + internal smoke
```
Jordan Green: About eval-triggered alerts — we should define the evaluation signals. I propose: concordance (exact-match where relevant), n-gram overlap, and a model-agnostic fallthrough score. Hold alerts at two severities: warning (auto-create PR/issue) and critical (auto-fallback to higher-fidelity model).
Maria G.: Example alert config sketch: 
```
alerts:
  trigger: eval_threshold
  eval_set: "concordance_v2"
  threshold: 0.92
  severity: ["warning","critical"]
  actions:
    - warning: create-ticket
    - critical: route-to-model: "redwood-large-compat"
```
Lee: Need ops runbook text for fallback — who owns the fallback? automatic fallback path should be opt-in per-deployment for Dedicated/Private customers. Hosted can default to auto-fallback with notify.
Alice K: We should add a required acceptance metric: no more than 2% user-visible quality regressions in pilot traffic after enabling quant recommendations. measure via A/B.
Sam Li: +1. Also we need a UX microflow for SEs: 1) see econ estimate, 2) opt-in quant profile or auto-apply with rollback, 3) run quick eval against saved prompt set. This reduces support churn.
Maria G.: Implementation thoughts: product will own guidance surface + Console bits; infra owns autoset and routing; runtime owns safe-quant kernels and metrics tagging. I'll add owners in the draft PR.
ops-bot: Deploy note: scheduled window requested for alpha rollout — 2026-04-07 02:00 UTC. react with :thumbsup: to approve.
Jordan Green: Action items from this thread:
- Maria: publish strawman doc and owners (deadline Thu)
- Sam: mockups for econ estimator + microflow (deadline Mon)
- Lee: ops runbook skeleton + fallback policy draft (deadline Tue)
- Alice: define pilot acceptance A/B metrics and eval sets (deadline Tue)
- All: thumbs up on the alpha rollout window by EOD today
Maria G.: Thanks — I'll push the doc to https://redwood.internal/docs/inference-efficiency-strawman and tag folks. If no objections, I'll start scheduling syncs with infra/runtime next week. :white_check_mark:
